chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you supplicates, let him be inclusive (of God's mercy/attributes), for it obligates (the response) for the supplication.'

key_terms.أَوْجَبُ: Obligates or makes more certain, indicating a stronger likelihood of acceptance
key_terms.يَعُمَّ: To be inclusive or comprehensive, referring to encompassing God's mercy or attributes in supplication

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'inclusive' in supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizing that 'ya'ummu' refers to generalizing the supplication to encompass all of God's beautiful names and attributes, thereby broadening the scope of divine mercy. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that inclusive supplication aligns the supplicant's intent with the totality of divine generosity, making the request more likely to be accepted.
